items.headline: Exclusive: US military had close call after using AI for false intelligence report, sources say
items.dek: The intelligence report, circulated across the US military this spring in the midst of the war with Iran, immediately set off alarm bells: A Chinese ship in the Middle East was transporting components of a nuclear weapons program.
items.author: Katie Bo Lillis, Zachary Cohen
items.caption: CNN headline, byline and photo of silhouetted US soldiers training with drones
items.notes: VERIFIED what happened: a SOCOM analyst used an AI chatbot on intel about a Chinese ship's manifest (reporting originated with US Special Operations Command Pacific); the bot fused OSINT with classified SIGINT and wrongly concluded the ship carried nuclear-weapons-program components; analyst used AI again to package it into a standard intel report. Armed US personnel were preparing to board; military planes were in the air; caught 'only just before the planned operation'. Source: report was “entirely false” but “almost started a war.” CNN could not learn what the misidentified cargo was, nor whether the chatbot was commercial or government. It was NOT a ship 'delivering nukes' - the claim was nuclear-weapons-program components, bound for/related to Iran during the 2026 Iran war.

items.headline: Clarifying “Responsible AI” at the DoW — Out with Utopian Idealism, In with Hard-Nosed Realism.

The Department must also utilize models free from usage policy constraints that may limit lawful military applications. ... I direct the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment to incorporate standard “any lawful use” language into any DoW contract through which AI services are procured within 180 days.

items.headline: GTG-87001: Disrupting a Yemen-based guided weapons engineering cell using Claude to develop guidance software
items.dek: We identified a cell of threat actors based in northern Yemen running three weapons development programs: a guided rocket that used a commodity phone-class flight computer with final-phase homing guidance; a multi-stage ballistic missile with a stated range goal above 2,000 km; and a multi-variant missile (referred to as the “R2000” set) that included a hypersonic glide vehicle variant.
items.caption: Crop of report page 112: case title and summary
items.notes: CORRECTION to outline: not an ICBM. Report says multi-stage ballistic missile with range goal >2,000 km (its table calls the variants 'Medium- and intermediate-range and hypersonic-glide'). Anthropic says 'northern Yemen' and does not name the Houthis; media (FT via Middle East Eye) note the area is largely Houthi-controlled. No 'logs' are published - the report gives narrative + a systems-engineering diagram, not chat transcripts.

items.headline: GTG-87001 (continued)
items.dek: The actors used Claude Code in place of human software engineers to develop the guidance, navigation, and control (GNC) software that steers and stabilizes a flying vehicle. ... Our safeguards blocked many of their requests, but not all of them. ... We do not have evidence the actors succeeded in fielding an operational device; but they did test-fire a guided rocket. This field test appears to have failed: within hours, the actors returned to Claude to work out why it failed.
items.caption: Crop of report page 113: Claude Code as the cell's engineering team, safeguards partly evaded, failed rocket test
items.notes: The 'unsuccessful attempts' in the outline = the failed guided-rocket test-fire. Actors ran several Claude instances as a mini engineering team (coder, researcher, reviewer) and split work across sessions to hide intent; they also built an offline simulation toolkit that no longer needs Claude.

items.headline: Case 1: Development - Guided-weapons engineering cell on the systems development lifecycle
items.dek: Figure 1. The systems engineering V for the GNC cell ... Tactical guided rocket: A live field test in Yemen, brought back to Claude for failure analysis within hours. Ballistic missile simulation: Medium- and intermediate-range and hypersonic-glide variants.
items.caption: Official figure: systems-engineering V showing how far Claude carried each of the three Yemeni weapons programs (rocket reached flight test), plus summary table
items.notes: Rendered at 250 dpi from the PDF.

items.headline: Disrupting the first reported AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign
items.dek: The threat actor—whom we assess with high confidence was a Chinese state-sponsored group—manipulated our Claude Code tool into attempting infiltration into roughly thirty global targets and succeeded in a small number of cases.
items.caption: Anthropic blog headline and date (GTG-1002)
items.notes: 'the threat actor was able to use AI to perform 80-90% of the campaign, with human intervention required only sporadically (perhaps 4-6 critical decision points per hacking campaign)'. Diagram: anthropic-gtg1002-attack-lifecycle.png. (Security group may also use this.)

items.headline: Detecting and countering misuse of AI: August 2025
items.dek: Our Threat Intelligence report discusses several recent examples of Claude being misused, including a large-scale extortion operation using Claude Code, a fraudulent employment scheme from North Korea, and the sale of AI-generated ransomware by a cybercriminal with only basic coding skills.
items.caption: Anthropic blog headline and date
items.notes: 'Vibe hacking': actor targeted at least 17 organizations (healthcare, emergency services, government, religious institutions), ransoms sometimes exceeding $500,000. North Korea: operatives used Claude to get and keep remote jobs at US Fortune 500 tech companies; 'Operators who cannot otherwise write basic code or communicate professionally in English are now able to pass technical interviews'.

items.headline: Virology Capabilities Test
items.dek: VCT is difficult: expert virologists with access to the internet score an average of 22.1% on questions specifically in their sub-areas of expertise. However, the most performant LLM, OpenAI’s o3, reaches 43.8% accuracy and even outperforms 94% of expert virologists when compared directly on question subsets specifically tailored to the experts’ specialties.
items.caption: VCT site with results table: o3 43.8% (94th percentile of experts) vs expert virologists 22.1%
items.notes: Paper: arXiv:2504.16137 (Götting et al., incl. Dan Hendrycks). TIME's exclusive on this (time.com/7279010) blocked the headless browser. Numbers also in datasets.

facts.claim: The memo orders the latest frontier AI models deployed to the military within 30 days of public release, and “any lawful use” language in every AI contract within 180 days.
Memo: “We must approach risk tradeoffs, 'equities', and other subjective questions as if we were at war.” A monthly “Barrier Removal Board” may waive non-statutory requirements.
Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and xAI each received Pentagon contracts worth up to $200 million for 'frontier AI' in July 2025.

After Anthropic refused to allow Claude for mass domestic surveillance or fully autonomous weapons, Hegseth declared it a “supply chain risk to national security” — a label Anthropic says was “historically reserved for US adversaries.”
Anthropic: “we do not believe that today’s frontier AI models are reliable enough to be used in fully autonomous weapons.”
A federal appeals court upheld the Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic 2-1 on Sept 25, 2026.
Israel's 'Lavender' AI system marked about 37,000 Gazans as potential targets.
In a King's College London study, AI models chose nuclear escalation in 95% of simulated war games; “no model ever chose accommodation or withdrawal even when under acute pressure.”
Trump on AI regulation: “The only control or 'guardrails' that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!” ... “WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS!”

facts.claim: Trump: “The robots will not be taking over. The AI will not be taking over the rest of the world. The whole thing is a hoax.”

Trump at the Xi summit: “We're leading by at least a year, maybe a year and a half. Some people say two years.” The US and China agreed a channel for AI-related incidents and an AI dialogue in November.
Dec 11, 2025: Trump signed an executive order to preempt state AI laws, creating a DOJ task force to sue states.
Dec 2025: Trump allowed Nvidia H200 sales to China in exchange for a 25% cut to the US government.
DeepSeek's R1 release wiped $589 billion off Nvidia's market value in one day — the largest single-day loss in stock market history.

A northern-Yemen cell used Claude Code “in place of human software engineers” to build missile guidance software for a guided rocket, a >2,000 km multi-stage ballistic missile and a hypersonic-glide variant; their rocket test failed and “within hours, the actors returned to Claude to work out why it failed.”

A Russia-based freelance team used Claude Code to build an autonomous FPV kamikaze drone swarm whose onboard model could select targets (including a “person” target class) and issue detonation commands without a human in the loop.

Anthropic's Sept 2026 threat report details state-linked researchers using Claude on dual-use biology (gain-of-function virology, avian-flu mammalian adaptation, venom/toxin design) via reseller relays that evaded regional blocks and rerouted refused prompts to more permissive models.
